raw_case_text:
A 34-year-old previously healthy male presented with high grade fever associated with constitutional symptoms of five days' duration. He was complaining of right hypochondrium pain and tea-coloured urine for two days associated with yellowish discolouration of the eyes. He had severe loss of appetite to food and water, but his bowel habits had been normal throughout the illness. On admission, he was afebrile with normal vital signs but was deeply icteric. His abdominal examination revealed a tender, mild hepatomegaly while his cardiovascular, respiratory, and nervous system examination was normal.
His full blood count revealed a white cell count of 3 x 103 muL with a platelet count of 116 x 103 muL. His aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) were 5162 U/L and 3964 U/L, respectively. Initial total bilirubin was found to be 61.7 mumol/L with an increased direct fraction. His prothrombin time/international normalized ratio (PT/INR) and serum protein were normal throughout the illness. His dengue IgM antibody done by chromatographic immunoassay was positive on the 6th day of the illness. Hepatitis A IgM antibody done by the ELISA technique was positive on day 6 of the illness, while hepatitis A IgG antibody was negative. Other investigations done during the hospital stay are summarized in Table 1.
During the course of the illness, the patient was closely monitored for features of development of liver failure while continuing with the precritical monitoring of the dengue fever. The patient's hospital stay was uneventful, and he did not develop features of acute liver failure or features of plasma leakage as in DHF. He was discharged on day 10 of the illness. On follow-up, his AST, ALT, and bilirubin have become normal.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old male presented with a 5-day history of high-grade fever and constitutional symptoms, and a 2-day history of right hypochondrial pain, tea-colored urine, scleral icterus, and severe anorexia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy man developed 5 days of high-grade fever with constitutional symptoms, followed 2 days prior to admission by right upper quadrant abdominal pain, dark tea-colored urine, yellowing of the eyes, and profound loss of appetite for food and water.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 5-day high-grade fever, constitutional symptoms, right hypochondrial pain, tea-colored urine, scleral icterus, and severe anorexia. Normal bowel habits.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile on admission with normal vital signs, deep scleral and cutaneous icterus, and tender mild hepatomegaly; cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological examinations were normal, with no clinical signs of hepatic encephalopathy or plasma leakage.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission FBC showed leukopenia (WBC 3 x 10^3/uL) and mild thrombocytopenia (platelets 116 x 10^3/uL). Liver panel revealed marked transaminitis with AST 5,162 U/L and ALT 3,964 U/L, total bilirubin 61.7 umol/L (predominantly direct hyperbilirubinemia), and normal prothrombin time/INR and serum protein throughout hospitalization. Hepatitis A IgM ELISA was positive on day 6 of illness (with negative hepatitis A IgG).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Concurrent acute dengue fever and acute viral hepatitis A coinfection presenting with severe transaminitis (AST >5,000 U/L, ALT >3,900 U/L) without acute liver failure or plasma leakage, confirmed on day 6 of illness by positive dengue IgM chromatographic immunoassay and positive hepatitis A IgM ELISA. Managed supportively with close hepatic and dengue pre-critical monitoring, discharged uneventfully on day 10 of illness, and achieved complete normalization of AST, ALT, and bilirubin on outpatient follow-up.
